intent.expectation: feasible for roughly a third of seeds; the rest are unknown rather than proven infeasible
intent.exercises: contention for yard capacity under a tight arrival rate, with composition length deliberately taken out of the picture
notes: Material is restricted to the four shortest types, exactly as in feasible_small, so with units_per_composition [1,2] the longest train is 138.7 m and nothing here can ever fail on length. Whatever varies with the seed is contention, not size.

min_gap_on_gateway is 300 s against a 180-450 s move off the gateway, so an arriving train frequently cannot clear the track before the next one needs it. Arrival times are drawn without replacement from a 300 s grid over the first half of the horizon, giving 18 slots for 14 trains, so how tightly they cluster is up to the seed. These numbers were tuned empirically: 6 trains at 450 s was feasible for all of seeds 1-20, i.e. not marginal at all.

The observed failure mode was not the one this config was designed around. It was expected to strand trains on the gateway (Robust-Rail-NL/robust-rail-solver#13), but across seeds 1-20 not one failure was a gateway wait. Instead the solver overfills track 906b, a 255 m stub behind a buffer stop, and then cannot get trains back out: 'exceeds the maximum length', 'One side is blocked by another train', 'Both sides blocked'. That is the ordinary difficulty of a dead-end parking track, which makes this a better congestion fixture than intended — it does not depend on a known bug.
Failures are classified 'unknown', which is the honest verdict: the solver found no valid plan, but a heuristic failing to find one does not prove none exists. Several of these may well be plannable.
